messages:
violet: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a tiny post-score 'tiebreaker qualifier' stage to nudge decisions between latency/cost/region. Goals: tiny runtime cost, auditable, and per-tenant opt-in.

dan: Sounds sensible. Two immediate concerns: hotspotting if deterministic, and telemetry for explainability. We should default to deterministic but offer a seeded_hash mode to spread load.

reza: Agree. Implementation sketch: small micro-DSL compiled at control-plane -> bytecode loaded into sidecar. Modes: deterministic | seeded_hash | round_robin. Seeded_hash takes tenant_id+request_id to distribute.

violet: Runtime contract: pure function, no syscalls, 100-200us budget, idempotent. If it errs or times out runtime applies neutral semantics (no-op) and increments qualifier.failure counter.

dan: Telemetry proposal: emit qualifier.{tenant}.{id}.applied (bool), qualifier.{tenant}.{id}.delta_score (histogram), qualifier.{tenant}.{id}.mode. Also include qualifier.explain field in trace where we log original_score -> adjusted_score.

reza: Validation: control-plane should static-analyze DSL for unsafe ops, constant-fold, and reject expressions referencing external signals. Provide safe-list of ops (add,mul,clamp,lerp,seeded_hash). Also include a version tag so we can alter semantics later.

violet: Example micro-config for RFC notes (compact):
```
qualifier_id: tie_seed_v1
version: "1"
mode: seeded_hash
expr: "score + bias * (region_pref - cost_norm)"
params: bias=0.07
```

dan: Rollout: 1) feature-flag in control-plane UI 2) sidecar-only for internal tenants 3) 48-72h sim + smoke in low-traffic prod tenants 4) opt-in for customers. Central-router implementation can come later if we need to consolidate.

reza: Tests: unit evals, microbench (p95 eval latency), sim harness for traffic shapes, chaos test where evaluator throws -> confirm neutral fallback. Also add regression test to ensure seeded_hash actually evens out hot keys.

violet: Ops/alerts: watch qualifier.failure_rate > 0.5% and qualifier.applied_rate deviation > 10% from baseline. Add runbook steps for rollback: flip tenant flag off -> restart sidecar if stuck.

dan: One more: affinity cap idea. If qualifier repeatedly picks same backend and we observe load skew, we should apply an automatic temporary cap per-backend for that tenant for N minutes. Add as future follow-up.

reza: +1 on affinity cap follow-up. For now keep qualifier simple and observable. I'll prototype bytecode emitter and seeded_hash function.

sre-bot: deploy-notice: branch qualifier-tie-shim pushed to staging (https://redwood-infra/changes/qualifier-tie-shim) :rocket:

violet: Great. I'll write a short addendum with schema, telemetry names, and the staged rollout checklist. @dan @reza please add perf numbers and a prototype by EOD.
